purpose: Methodologically safe quantitative evidence extraction backlog and challenge-aligned action translation gates; no new effect sizes

records.findingAsRecorded: Pooled data from five bed-rest control cohorts (50 men, 24 women) with durations of 14–90 days.
records.limitations: Non-randomized pooled cohorts; heterogeneous durations; not direct spaceflight evidence.

records.findingAsRecorded: Urinary NTX, CTX, HP and PYD excretion increased during bed rest in both sexes; creatinine normalization removed sex differences but not the bed-rest increase.
records.measurementContext: urinary collagen crosslinks; creatinine-normalized results discussed separately
records.limitations: Do not equate urinary CTX with serum CTX assays or infer percentage bone loss.

records.sourceLocator: Results: renal stone risk; urine chemistry discussion
records.findingAsRecorded: Urinary calcium and oxalate excretion increased, while urinary citrate and pH decreased during bed rest; high fluid intake in the study limited observed stone risk.
records.measurementContext: urine chemistry; not observed clinical stone incidence
records.limitations: Do not calculate individual kidney stone probability; fluid intake and diet confound interpretation.

records.sourceLocator: Abstract; Results: bone density and renal stone risk
records.findingAsRecorded: Authors report broadly similar skeletal unloading responses across sexes, with site-specific exceptions in femoral-neck BMD.
records.limitations: Sex-specific exceptions and variable study duration preclude universal sex-independent claims.

requiredBeforeQuantitativeClaim: accessible full text and exact table/figure/section locator
specimen and assay identity including units
effect estimate and uncertainty exactly transcribed

translationToAstronautGuidance.gather: source, timestamp, unit, specimen, device/assay and data-quality metadata required
translationToAstronautGuidance.evaluate: personal baseline and study population applicability must be distinguished; never equate bed rest analog with astronaut-specific risk
translationToAstronautGuidance.act: reference-only contextual explanation; no diagnosis, dose, treatment, automated alert or unapproved recommendation
translationToAstronautGuidance.followUp: show missing data, request remeasurement when appropriate under mission protocol, or refer to qualified flight medical staff; not autonomous medical direction
